doubts.claim_under_doubt: a fold never breaks the integrity gate, including when the release is later aborted
doubts.disproof_attempt: A release PR now contains the fold commit; reverting a merged release (git revert -m1, or a squash-merged release) deletes the archive that exists at the merge-base, which check_integrity flags as deleted_existing. No event is lost, but the revert is blocked. Nothing in the skill or docs says to leave the chore(events) commit out of a revert.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Document that reverting a release reverts only the chore(release) commit, not the fold commit.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: a fold never loses an event and the step can never stop a release
doubts.disproof_attempt: _rollback deletes the new archive even when its own reset or checkout failed (index.lock from a hook timeout or another session). The work tree then holds neither the folded drops nor the archive, the index keeps the drop deletions staged, Step 6 fails on index.lock, and Step 7's staged-diff pathspec could commit the deletions without the archive.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Delete the archive only after the tracked drops are confirmed back; document the repair for rolled_back false and a left-behind index.lock.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: the fold commit always passes the events integrity check
doubts.disproof_attempt: plan_fold judges merged against the trunk TIP while check_integrity judges against merge-base(trunk, HEAD). A release branch whose own old drop was squash-merged into the trunk but never rebased makes the archive look injected.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: an aborted release leaves no trace
doubts.disproof_attempt: If Step 5.5 refuses, the chore(events) commit stays and may be read into the changelog on the re-run.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Skip chore(events) commits in Step 2, or confirm chore commits are dropped.
